label: Active stand test
definition: Ten-minute active standing with serial heart rate and blood pressure, the pragmatic clinic alternative to tilt. Yields a different heart-rate increment than tilt, which matters for phenotype threshold portability.

label: Ambulatory heart rate and blood pressure monitoring
definition: Holter, patch electrocardiography, wearable heart-rate and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure. The realistic source of a heart-rate criterion in routine electronic health record data, as opposed to a formal lab.

label: Autoimmune evidence
definition: Autoantibodies against autonomic targets (ganglionic acetylcholine receptor, adrenergic and muscarinic receptors) or a coexisting systemic autoimmune disease.

label: Autonomic autoantibody assay
definition: Ganglionic acetylcholine receptor antibody, and adrenergic and muscarinic receptor antibody panels including functional cell-based assays.

label: Beta blockade
definition: Propranolol, metoprolol, bisoprolol and related agents, most often given on a hyperadrenergic rationale.

label: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing
definition: Peak oxygen uptake, chronotropic response and ventilatory efficiency, the objective substrate for the deconditioning flag and for post-exertional malaise phenotyping.

label: Central sympatholytics
definition: Clonidine and methyldopa, reserved almost exclusively for a hyperadrenergic presentation and therefore an unusually specific proxy.

label: Cerebral blood flow velocity
definition: Transcranial Doppler middle-cerebral-artery velocity, near-infrared spectroscopy, or cerebral oximetry during orthostasis. Explains symptoms that the heart-rate criterion does not.

label: Migraine and chronic headache
definition: Migraine, chronic daily headache and their overlap with orthostatic headache from cerebral hypoperfusion or cerebrospinal fluid leak.

label: Compression garments
definition: Abdominal binders and lower-limb compression that mechanically oppose venous pooling, targeting the neuropathic and hypovolemic flags.

label: Deconditioning evidence
definition: Reduced cardiac mass and stroke volume with low peak oxygen uptake, whether as primary cause or as a secondary consequence of activity avoidance. Its causal direction is contested, which is exactly why it is a flag and not a subtype.

label: Competing orthostatic diagnoses
definition: Vasovagal syncope, neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, inappropriate sinus tachycardia and pure autonomic failure. Exclusion of these is part of the POTS definition, so a computable phenotype needs them explicitly.

label: Droxidopa
definition: Noradrenaline prodrug used where a peripheral noradrenergic deficit is suspected.

label: Exercise reconditioning
definition: Structured recumbent-to-upright exercise programmes such as the Levine and CHOP protocols, prescribed against a deconditioning hypothesis.

label: Genetic testing
definition: Variant testing relevant to POTS and its comorbidities: noradrenaline transporter (SLC6A2), mast-cell and tryptase loci, and connective-tissue genes.

label: Gastrointestinal dysmotility
definition: Gastroparesis, chronic constipation and rapid gastric emptying, reflecting enteric autonomic involvement.

label: Head-up tilt table test
definition: Passive 60-70 degree head-up tilt with continuous heart rate and blood pressure. Supplies the diagnostic heart-rate increment itself.

label: Heart rate variability and baroreflex sensitivity
definition: Spectral and time-domain heart-rate variability, deep-breathing respiratory sinus arrhythmia, and baroreflex gain: the cardiovagal side of autonomic testing.

label: Hyperadrenergic evidence
definition: Excess sympathetic outflow or impaired noradrenaline clearance: upright plasma noradrenaline elevation, marked orthostatic hypertension, tremor and cold sweaty extremities, or a noradrenaline transporter deficiency.

label: Joint hypermobility and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
definition: Generalised joint hypermobility or hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, offered as a mechanism for increased venous compliance and pooling.

label: Hypovolemic evidence
definition: Reduced plasma or red-cell volume, frequently with a paradoxically low plasma renin activity and aldosterone for the degree of volume depletion.

label: Immunomodulation
definition: Intravenous immunoglobulin, rituximab, plasma exchange and corticosteroids given for a presumed autoimmune mechanism.

label: Ivabradine
definition: Selective sinoatrial funny-current inhibitor, lowering heart rate without lowering blood pressure. Signals a rate-centred rather than volume-centred hypothesis.

label: Long COVID and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2
definition: POTS arising after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The subject of the Larsen deep phenotyping study, and the reason the modern incident cohort exists.

label: Mast cell activation syndrome
definition: Mast cell activation disorder with flushing, and raised tryptase or urinary methylhistamine, which can mimic or amplify a hyperadrenergic picture.

label: ME/CFS and post-exertional malaise
definition: Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome, sharing orthostatic intolerance and post-exertional malaise with POTS.

label: Midodrine
definition: Alpha-1 agonist vasoconstrictor, used where venous pooling or neuropathic vasoconstrictor failure is suspected.

label: Neuropathic evidence
definition: Peripheral autonomic denervation, typically a length-dependent small-fibre and sudomotor deficit producing impaired lower-limb vasoconstriction and venous pooling.

label: Plasma and blood volume measurement
definition: Direct volume quantification by carbon monoxide rebreathing, indocyanine green, or iodinated-albumin dilution. The only way to make the hypovolemic flag objective rather than inferred.

label: Supine and upright plasma catecholamines
definition: Paired supine and standing noradrenaline and adrenaline. An upright noradrenaline above roughly 600 pg/mL is the most-cited hyperadrenergic criterion, and the paired design is what makes it interpretable.

label: Post-vaccination onset
definition: Symptom onset temporally associated with vaccination, principally human papillomavirus and SARS-CoV-2 vaccines. Recorded because it appears in the literature as a claimed trigger and any phenotype must be able to identify and stratify these reports rather than silently absorb them.

label: Post-infectious evidence
definition: Symptom onset temporally linked to an infection, including SARS-CoV-2, Epstein-Barr virus, influenza and Lyme disease.

label: Pyridostigmine
definition: Peripheral acetylcholinesterase inhibitor enhancing ganglionic transmission, used on a neuropathic or autoimmune rationale.

label: QSART and sudomotor testing
definition: Quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test and related sympathetic sweat measures. Zhang et al. found reduced sweat output in about a third of 356 patients tested.

label: Serotonergic and other central agents
definition: Serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors and modafinil. Deliberately kept as a low-specificity facet, since these are also prescribed for coexisting depression, anxiety and fatigue rather than for any orthostatic mechanism.

label: Skin biopsy and intraepidermal nerve fibre density
definition: Punch biopsy with PGP 9.5 immunostaining and nerve-fibre density quantification, the structural counterpart to sudomotor testing. Zhang et al. reported reduced density in about 24% of those biopsied.

label: Small fibre neuropathy diagnosis
definition: Small fibre neuropathy as a recorded diagnosis rather than as a test result. Held separately from the neuropathic mechanism flag because in electronic health record data the diagnosis code and the biopsy result are different observations with different reliability.

label: Sjogren and other systemic autoimmune disease
definition: Coexisting systemic autoimmune disease: Sjogren syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, coeliac disease, autoimmune thyroiditis.

label: Thermoregulatory sweat test
definition: Whole-body sweat distribution under controlled heating, localising anhidrosis and distinguishing pre- from post-ganglionic lesions when read against QSART.

label: Valsalva manoeuvre
definition: Valsalva ratio and phase II/IV blood-pressure response, separating adrenergic from cardiovagal failure. Part of the standard autonomic reflex screen alongside deep breathing and QSART.

label: Volume expansion therapy
definition: Fludrocortisone, salt and fluid loading, desmopressin, and intravenous saline. Prescription implies a clinician's hypovolemic hypothesis.
